item.text: {"summary":"Fix hexadecimal escaping before a following hexadecimal digit.","explanation":"In `CEscape.EscapeAndUnescape`, the input contains byte 0x02 followed by ASCII `3`. The assertion at line 76 reports `unescaped_str` as `\"foo\\nxx\\r\\b#\"`, while `original` contains 0x02 followed by `3`. At line 86, in-place output `s` has the same observed value and differs from the same `original`. `CEscapeInternal` tests the wrong condition: it escapes a following character when it is not a hex digit, so the literal `3` remains after `\\x02`. `CUnescape` then consumes it as part of the hex escape and produces `#` (0x23). Escaping a following hex digit restores the round-trip contract for both normal and in-place unescaping.","edits":[{"path":"absl/strings/escaping.cc","old":"(!absl::ascii_isprint(uc) ||\n             (last_hex_escape && !absl::ascii_isxdigit(uc)))","new":"(!absl::ascii_isprint(uc) ||\n             (last_hex_escape && absl::ascii_isxdigit(uc)))"}]}
